Team Name: Creative Cosmos
Team Number: 11593
Division: Elementary
How does the amount of moon regolith affect how much a plant will grow?
We think that the more earth soil in the pot mixture, the better the plant will grow. We don’t predict that any of
the plants in pots with 50% or higher moon regolith compositions will grow a plant at all.
A second question our team wanted to investigate was do water beads require you to water a plant less often?
We were hoping the water beads would help solve the problem of water scarcity on the moon as water is a
critical component to grow plants. We had done some research on water beads and it sounded like we
wouldn’t need as much water to grow plants if these were evenly mixed into the soil mixture. We were worried
that the water beads could kill the plant due to chemicals and that seemed to happen. By week 6, all three of
our pots that had water beads mixed into the soil were looking sickly and turning more brown. The control pots
that had the same plant and same soil mixture composition were looking much healthier.
In week two of the grow period, all of our plants were growing, even those in 100% moon regolith. Since we
had extra regolith left, we planted 7 more pots this time using different plants in each one since we had already
learned that the moon regolith would actually grow a plant. Now we wanted to dig deeper and see if certain
vegetable plants would grow better in the moon regolith than others.
The independent variables in our experiment are the percentage of regulant (moon dust) to soil and the pots
with water beads (sodium polyacrylate).
The dependent variable in our experiment is plant growth.
The controls in our experiment are the type of seed, amount of water, time under grow lights, and the same
amount of measured soil/regolith in each pot.
We took measurements of the plants height, how much water was given, the plants moisture level, the ph and
also the leaf count of each plant every week and logged it into our notebook. We have included pictures of the
weekly charting and data in our weekly pictures if you zoom in but will also include some pics of the notebook
separately to see a more close up.
The results of our experiment shocked us. We grew real green beans that we were able to harvest. Plus all of
our vegetable plants grew in all 15 pots. The green bean plant and the lima bean plant had the most
astonishing growth in the grow period and we started them one week into the grow period so they only had 7
weeks to grow. Once we realized that some of the plants we planted in week 2 were overtaking the growth rate
of the original radish seeds, we posed a new question: Which plant will grow the tallest?

The clear winner of the challenge was the lima bean plant. It grew the tallest. One of the coolest unexpected
things that we didn’t realize could happen was that the green bean plant started growing green beans! We
picked them after the grow period ended and put them in some pictures to see. The green bean was the clear
winner of choice to plant on the moon from all of the vegetables we tested as it grew green beans in only 7
weeks and you want a plant that will grow food quickly when you have limited food available.
